overview: This bill writes the "Rule of Two" into the Small Business Act. Under this rule, when a federal contract is expected to be worth more than the simplified acquisition threshold (the dollar level above which full purchasing procedures apply), the contracting officer must set it aside for small businesses only, if they reasonably expect at least two qualified small businesses to bid and the contract can be awarded at a fair market price. The bill does not apply the rule to task orders or delivery orders, which are orders placed under existing broader contracts. Putting the rule into law would make it harder for agencies to change or skip it through their own policies. As of July 2, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say putting the Rule of Two into law guarantees small businesses a fair shot at federal contracts, which supports competition and local jobs.
against: Critics say a firm set-aside requirement limits agencies' flexibility to choose the best value from any company, and excluding task and delivery orders leaves a large share of federal spending outside the rule.
